Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (VeraCommerce Head of Platform), Markus Klein (SRE), Priya Desai (CTO)

Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Quick sync on pilot telemetry, discussion of canary gating thresholds, blue/green cutover orchestration, and next steps for live smoke. Agreement to produce a runbook and schedule low-traffic canary window. Customer will share extra telemetry and traces.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, good to see you. Quick check - agenda is runbook review, canary gating, and telemetry gaps. Anything to add?
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: No, that's perfect. We mostly want to nail the traffic safety part — last week's spike freaked Mark us out, so yeah.
[00:20] Markus Klein: yeah the spike made some of our upstream latency visible. We want to avoid cascading alarms during cutover.
[00:30] Ravi Patel: Cool. I'll go quickly through what we changed this week: prefix caching enabled for two pilot routes, KV cache warmup script ran, and we tuned batch sizes down to favor p95 latency.
[00:40] Markus Klein: the batch changes looked good, p50 improved but p95 was the real winner. Our concern is tail when we shift traffic.
[00:50] Priya Desai: Priya here — just want confirmation: blue/green means we can flip traffic at the router level and fallback to previous green if thresholds cross?
[00:58] Maya Chen: Exactly. Our recommendation is a gradual traffic ramp (5% increments) with SLO-gated holds. If p95 latency > 2.5s or error-rate > 1% for a 5-minute window, we automatically pause and roll back.
[01:15] Lena Ortiz: That 2.5s number — that's for the entire end-to-end request, right? Not just token generation?
[01:20] Ravi Patel: It's end-to-end as measured by your tracing header — Redwood Console will compute token time + network hop times if you forward traces. We can also surface model time and infra time separately.
[01:34] Markus Klein: Can you break down what metrics we should watch in the first 15 minutes?
[01:38] Ravi Patel: Sure. Primary: p95 latency, 99th if you want extra caution, error-rate (5xx + model rejections), and KV-cache hit-rate. Secondary: token cost per request, output quality score — we run prompt-based checks to surface hallucination regressions.
[01:52] Maya Chen: Also add request volume and upstream queue length. We'll map those to gating rules in the runbook.
[02:00] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[02:06] Lena Ortiz: On the hallucination checks, how do you compute that? Is it the Redwood evals or our own golden prompts?
[02:12] Ravi Patel: Good question. We recommend a hybrid: Redwood provides sentinel prompt suite that flags likely regressions; you should add your domain-specific golden prompts — we'll run them as smoke tests during canary traffic and in the CI harness.
[02:26] Priya Desai: Are those golden prompts run on every canary increment? That's extra load.
[02:31] Ravi Patel: We run them with shadow traffic or sampled requests; just enough to get a statistically meaningful signal without spiking cost. Typical config is 1% of requests plus 200 synthetic golden prompts per step.
[02:45] Maya Chen: We're hearing a question about cost — yes, there's an incremental cost for smoke prompts. We can show estimated token cost per canary window in the runbook.
[02:55] Markus Klein: On rollback, what's the fastest path? DNS swing, API gateway rule flip, or a weighted routing?
[03:02] Maya Chen: Weighted routing at the edge is the recommended path for minimal disruption. We support both CDN-level weighted splits and internal routing rules if you prefer service mesh.
[03:12] Lena Ortiz: For our infra, service mesh rules are easiest since we already do weighted splits in envoy.
[03:18] Ravi Patel: We'll provide the JSON snippet for envoy traffic shifting. Also note we'll keep the old model nodes warm for a 15-minute overlap so that if you roll back you don't have cold-starts.
[03:30] Markus Klein: Good. What about observability? We need the Redwood Console dashboards exported into our Grafana; do you support that?
[03:36] Ravi Patel: We have a Prometheus scrape endpoint for metric exports and an alerting rules YAML you can import. For traces, we emit OTLP — you can forward to your collector.
[03:46] Priya Desai: Can the runbook include the exact alert thresholds, prometheus exprs, and Grafana dashboard JSON?
[03:52] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll attach a runbook appendix with all that.
[03:56] [05:00] (brief side conversation about slide deck upload)
[05:06] Lena Ortiz: We had one more ask: data residency and logs. During pilot, retention is fine but for go-live we need customer-managed KMS and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[05:18] Maya Chen: For Private deployments we do KMS integrations and full audit logs. For this hosted pilot we can enable log-forwarding to your S3 with bucket-level encryption and also provide an audit log stream. We are SOC 2 compliant; if you need the attestation we'll share it.
[05:34] Markus Klein: Good. Can you also add an append to the runbook for compliance checks? If rollback is triggered we need ticketing hooks so our on-call is alerted and we keep a timeline.
[05:45] Ravi Patel: We'll add PagerDuty webhook examples and a short ticketing template.
[05:50] [10:01] 
[10:05] Priya Desai: I'd like to call out one edge case — if third-party downstream time spikes but model is fine, we don't want to roll back the model. Can the gating be model-only?
[10:16] Ravi Patel: Absolutely. Gates can reference model-only metrics (model inference time, model error codes) versus end-to-end. We'll make sure the canary JSON includes both model-only and end-to-end gates so you can choose.
[10:30] Lena Ortiz: On canary step sizes, suggested increments? 5/10/25/50?
[10:36] Maya Chen: Standard is 5% steps to 25% then bigger jumps, but we can customize. For high risk we'd do 2% increments. Also include a manual hold at 10% for human checks.
[10:48] Markus Klein: How long per step is typical? 5-10 mins?
[10:52] Ravi Patel: 5 minutes minimum, 10 minutes preferred to get a decent sample for p95. If traffic is low you'll want longer or synthetic traffic to get signal.
[11:05] Lena Ortiz: We'll plan for a 02:00-04:00 UTC window; that's our quietest. Aim for 2 hours to allow for troubleshooting and replays.
[11:12] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll propose 02:00-04:00 on 2026-12-07 and prep the runbook for that.
[11:20] [20:00] Ravi Patel: quick note — during the pilot we saw a KV-cache hit-rate dip during high variance requests; we shipped a warming script. Mark us, can you share specific endpoints where you saw cache churn?
[20:30] Markus Klein: /order/summary and /recommendations were the biggest churners. We'll provide 48 hours of traces.
[20:38] Ravi Patel: Great — warming those keys before shifting traffic will help tail latency. We'll include warmup step in the runbook.
[20:45] Maya Chen: Also, we'll provide a small canary model (quantized) as a fallback path that uses less GPU and lower cost. If the main model exceeds cost thresholds you can failover to it.
[20:58] Priya Desai: That helps. What's the quality delta?
[21:03] Ravi Patel: Usually minor but depends on prompts — we'll estimate Rouge/F1 delta on your golden prompt set during the smoke.
[21:12] Lena Ortiz: Ok. Any security blockers left to close?
[21:16] Maya Chen: We have the SSO SAML config pending — we'll send a checklist. Also need the IP allowlist for the canary window if you want to restrict to certain CIDRs.
[21:26] Markus Klein: We'll send the CIDRs. Also want confirmation that we can purge logs after X days per policy?
[21:32] Maya Chen: Yes, retention is configurable. We'll include retention settings in the appendix.
[21:38] [30:00] 
[30:05] Priya Desai: Wrap up — let's confirm deliverables. Maya to send runbook draft; Ravi to send dashboards and envoy JSON; Markus to send traces and CIDRs.
[30:18] Maya Chen: Correct. We'll aim to get the runbook to you by 2026-12-02 and the dashboard exports by 2026-12-03.
[30:26] Lena Ortiz: We'll try to get the traces by Monday 2026-12-01.
[30:30] Maya Chen: Great. Any other risks?
[30:35] Markus Klein: One small one: if we have a downstream outage during the window we may have to abort entirely. We should have a decision tree.
[30:42] Ravi Patel: We'll add a decision tree in the runbook — steps to abort, rollback, and postmortem template.
[30:50] [40:00] 
[40:10] Maya Chen: Ok final clarifications — for gating JSON we will include these fields: metric, expr, threshold, window, action (pause/rollback/alert), owner. We'll push that as a gist so you can wire it into your automation.
[40:24] Lena Ortiz: Perfect. Can you also include a minimal manual rollback command we can run from our CLI?
[40:31] Ravi Patel: Yes, we'll give an envoy route weight patch example and a single CLI call that triggers immediate rollback.
[40:38] Priya Desai: Thanks all. Looks good to me.
[40:42] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and runbook. Meeting adjourned.

Recap / Next steps (verbal):
- Redwood to share runbook draft and gating JSON by 2026-12-02.
- Redwood to export dashboards and provide envoy JSON + pagerduty hooks by 2026-12-03.
- VeraCommerce to provide traces, CIDR allowlist, and traffic logs by 2026-12-01.
- Schedule canary smoke: 2026-12-07 02:00-04:00 UTC.
